role.altitude: The refinery operator keeps walking rounds, gauging tanks, deciding setpoints, judging differences, planning isolations and coordinating shutdowns; copying readings and lab results into logsheets, compiling reports and working out volumes in spreadsheets shrink.
skills_to_grow: Working from the historian and rounds app instead of logsheets
role.ambitious_version: An operator who starts each shift with the unit's numbers already compiled and spends the time on the plant.

tasks.short: Copy control-room readings, walk rounds and read field gauges, record field readings, copy laboratory results, compile operating data and results into the daily report, and review and sign it.

steps.what: Operator copies control-room instrument readings onto the logsheet
Operator walks rounds and reads field gauges
Operator records the field instrument readings: on a paper rounds sheet typed into the logsheet today, entered once on the handheld during rounds after the change
Operator copies laboratory results into the logsheet
Operator compiles operating data and laboratory results into the daily report
Operator reviews the compiled daily report for anomalies: values against the unit's state, the rounds and the laboratory results
Operator signs the reviewed daily report for the shift supervisor

tasks.design: Control-room values come from the process historian, and laboratory results from the laboratory system, straight into a historian-based logsheet instead of being copied into a spreadsheet. Field readings are entered on a handheld during rounds, with limits that flag out-of-range values on the spot. The daily report is built from these records. Walking rounds and reviewing and signing the report stay with the operator. Rounds records show who read what and when; that use is agreed with the works council.

approvals.approved_version: The daily report with control-room, field and laboratory values exactly as reviewed by the operator in s6, signed once in the logsheet for the shift supervisor; any change needs a new review and signature.

tasks.previous_blocker: Spreadsheet logsheets with macros and paper rounds sheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Historian-based logsheets, laboratory links and rounds apps.
tasks.still_hard: Instruments not connected to the historian.
tasks.human_edge: Smelling or hearing a problem on rounds.

ambition.what: See field readings against limits during the round instead of at the end of the shift.

tasks.altitude: Much less copying; rounds and review stay.

reach.learn: Whether the report is ready at shift change.

evidence.claim: At a large chemical site, 40 production sites built digital rounds and 650,000 readings reached the historian in one year; no time saving reported.
A mining plant replaced Excel logsheets with historian-based logsheets and reported more than 1,500 hours a year freed; vendor case without method.
Logs and rounds record who did what and when and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: recording and compiling operating data for the shift; process control is outside.
Input contract for s1: the process historian, run by the plant's automation team, holds about 90% of control-room values; s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s4: laboratory results released in the laboratory system by the laboratory.

Rounds, review and signing keep their full time. s3 keeps 70 because each field reading is still read and entered by the operator, and only typing the paper sheet goes; s1 keeps 20 for values outside the historian; s5 keeps 30 for checking the built report.
unknowns: Share of field instruments read on rounds.
research_questions: Are out-of-range field readings acted on sooner?

already_counted.description: Operator rechecks readings the rounds app flags as out of range.

incremental.description: Operator reports wrong tag mappings in the logsheet.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many instruments are not connected and laboratory links are late, so half of the values are still copied (26.0); high: about 90% of values in the historian as assumed (41.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather the schedule, specifications, logs and laboratory results, analyze them to determine how to set equipment controls, discuss changes with the supervisor and laboratory, and note setpoint changes with reasons.

steps.what: Operator gathers the production schedule, product specifications, logs and latest laboratory results
Operator analyzes specifications, test results and laboratory recommendations to determine how to set equipment controls
Operator discusses changes with the shift supervisor and laboratory
Operator notes setpoint changes and reasons in the shift log

tasks.design: A shift dashboard shows the planned run targets, product specifications, the latest laboratory results against specification and recent log entries for the unit in one view, instead of collecting them from documents and spreadsheets. Analysing and deciding setpoints, and agreeing changes, stay with the operator; no software sets controls. Setpoint changes are taken from the control system into the shift log, and the operator adds the reason.
tasks.previous_blocker: Specifications, schedules and results sat in separate documents and systems.
tasks.enabler_now: Shift dashboards fed by planning, laboratory and historian data.
tasks.still_hard: Crude changes that behave differently from the plan.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing how this unit responds to a change.

reach.learn: Whether results are acted on sooner.

evidence.claim: AI is high-risk when it is a safety component in supplying gas, heating or electricity; dashboards and log entries are not.
A shift handover product links sensor data and field notes to the plant's historian.

assumptions: Boundary: deciding how to set controls for the shift; carrying out the changes is outside.
Input contract for s1: run targets from the planning system, specifications kept by the technology department, laboratory results from the laboratory system.
Analysis and discussion keep their full time.
unknowns: How often setpoints change per shift.

incremental.description: Operator reports missing or wrong data on the dashboard.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the dashboard lacks part of the data and crude changes need documents outside it, so half of the gathering stays (7.9); high: dashboard fed as assumed (16.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Join shutdown planning, determine isolation points and sequence, write up isolation lists and step plans, coordinate shutdowns and major projects with contractors and maintenance, and track task progress.

steps.what: Operator joins planning meetings for the shutdown
Operator determines isolation points and the shutdown sequence
Operator writes up isolation lists and step plans
Operator checks the final isolation lists and step plans against the decided isolations and the plant as it is now
Operator submits the checked isolation lists to management of change in the permit system
Operator coordinates shutdowns and major projects with contractors and maintenance on site
Maintenance staff and contractors close their tasks on the board as they finish
Operator tracks progress of shutdown tasks: in a spreadsheet chased by phone today, on the shared board after the change, and reports status in the shutdown meetings

tasks.design: Isolation lists and step plans start from the previous shutdown's lists kept in the permit system, so the operator edits instead of retyping, checks the final lists and submits them once. Determining isolations and sequence, and coordinating on site, stay with the operator. Shutdown tasks sit on a board in the maintenance planning system, and maintenance and contractors close tasks there, so status is read from the board instead of a spreadsheet. Changed isolation lists go through management of change.

approvals.approved_version: The isolation lists and step plans exactly as checked by the operator in s3b, submitted once to management of change in the permit system for this shutdown; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Lists were retyped for each shutdown and status chased by phone.
tasks.enabler_now: Permit systems with saved isolation lists and shared task boards.
tasks.still_hard: Surprises found when equipment is opened.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which valve passes and needs a blind.

evidence.claim: The safety management system covers operating procedures and management of change.
Saved lists and shared task boards replace retyping and status spreadsheets.

assumptions: Boundary: the operator's part of shutdowns and projects; maintenance work itself is outside.
Input contract for s3: isolation lists from the previous shutdown stored in the permit system.
Input contract for s5: maintenance and contractors close tasks on the board as they finish.

Meetings, isolations, coordination, the list check and the submission keep their full time. s3 keeps 60 because the previous lists are edited and changed points are still written; s5 keeps 50 because status is read from the board and still reported in meetings. Closing tasks on the board (s5c) is maintenance and contractor time, outside the operator's savings.

incremental.description: Operator updates stored isolation lists after plant changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the first shutdown of a changed unit, so stored lists fit little and contractors close tasks late (3.8); high: repeated shutdowns with stored lists (12.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gauge tanks and take samples, record readings, prepare calculations for receipts and deliveries of oil and oil products, check them against meter and ship figures, prepare, sign and send the quantity document.

steps.what: Gauger gauges the tank and takes samples for custody transfer

Gauger records level, temperature and density readings: by hand today; after the change automatic gauges feed level and temperature and the gauger enters the manual and density readings on the handheld
Gauger prepares calculations of standard volumes for receipts and deliveries
Gauger checks the quantities against meter and ship figures and judges differences
Gauger prepares the receipt or delivery quantity document
Gauger checks the final quantity document against the judged figures: product, tank, quantities and parties, and signs it
Gauger sends the signed document to the customer or ship agent

approvals.approved_version: The quantity document exactly as checked and signed by the gauger in s6, sent once to the customer or ship agent named on it; any change needs a new check and signature.

tasks.design: Tank radar gauges and temperature probes feed the tank management system, and manual custody-transfer readings are entered on a handheld. The system applies the standard volume correction tables and computes received or delivered quantities, instead of a spreadsheet with tables looked up by hand. Gauging, judging differences against meters and ship figures, and signing stay with the gauger. The quantity document is generated from the calculation, then signed and sent.
tasks.previous_blocker: Correction factors were looked up in tables and quantities worked out in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Tank management systems with automatic gauging and standard correction tables.
tasks.still_hard: Disputes over differences with ship figures.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a reading that does not fit the tank's history.
tasks.altitude: Much less calculating; gauging and judging stay.

evidence.claim: Gauging and temperature correction are fixed formulas that tank management systems can apply.
Refineries fall under NIS2, so a supplier reading plant data must be assessed.

assumptions: Boundary: quantity calculations and documents for receipts and deliveries; invoicing is outside.
Input contract for s2: automatic tank gauges, maintained by the instrument team, on about 80% of tanks; the rest are entered on the handheld; s2 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s3: the correction tables configured in the tank management system and checked after each update.

Gauging, judging and signing keep their full time. s2 keeps 60 because custody-transfer gauging and density readings are still read and entered by the gauger; s3 keeps 15 for checking the system's result; s5 keeps 30 for checking the generated document.
unknowns: Share of tanks with automatic gauges.

incremental.description: Gauger checks the system's calculation against a hand calculation after each table update.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mostly manual gauging and table updates that need checking, so most readings and many calculations stay by hand (19.7); high: about 80% of tanks gauged automatically as assumed (29.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
